narrator.who: Senior Curator Ellen Marsh, Geocomtex Collections

lines.n01: Everything in this room fell out of the sky. Your job is to make sure none of it ever leaves.
lines.n02: Geocomtex Collections. Level fifty three, half a mile under Utah. Senior Curator Ellen Marsh, recording the night staff induction.
lines.n03: Mr van Statten likes it dark when he isn't here. Lesson one: know where the switch is.
lines.n04: Welcome to the finest private collection of alien artefacts on Earth. Possibly the only one. That's in your contract, by the way.
lines.n05: Chunks of meteorite. And moon dust, sealed in nineteen sixty nine. Nobody opens that jar. Including me.
lines.n06: The milometer from the Roswell ship. It still counts. Just not in miles.
lines.n07: This arm came with an invoice that said Slitheen. We don't ask what it was attached to.
lines.n08: The egg is not an egg. Probably. Please don't tap the glass.
lines.n09: And our centrepiece. Found in the London sewers, nineteen seventy seven. Whatever wore this thought it was the future.
lines.n10: Every case is wired. One fingerprint on the glass, and the whole level seals itself.
lines.n11: Ninety seconds, floor to ceiling. Nothing gets in. Nothing gets out.
lines.n12: Which brings us down to the Cage. Our only living exhibit. Mr van Statten calls it the Metaltron. Nobody else calls it anything.
lines.n13: It doesn't eat. It doesn't sleep. It hasn't made a sound in three years. Don't talk to it. And don't stand where it can see you.
lines.n14: That's the tour. Lights out at midnight. If you hear anything down here, you didn't. Marsh, logging off.
lines.k1: Observation log. March the third. Subject still hasn't moved.
lines.k2: Eighteen hours now. It won't eat. It won't sleep. I don't think it needs to.
lines.k3: Mr van Statten wants it to speak. He says keep the lights on. Keep talking to it.
lines.k4: It isn't looking at me. It's looking at the camera.
